---
title: Pull and push
description: Write a vendor's records into Marfa as items, notice what people change there, and carry those changes back to the vendor.
---

A connector pulls: it reads the vendor and writes what it finds as items. A two-way connector also pushes: it notices what people change in Marfa and carries those changes back to the vendor.

The operations below come in the order a run uses them, for a connector built directly on the API. [The connector kit](/build/connector) does all of this for you.

The examples follow a task manager connector with a key of its own under the source `tasks`, which writes the type `tasks.task` with `link_field` `task_id`. In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a [TypeScript SDK](/typescript-sdk) client made with that key, `connectorId` is the registration's ID, and `processName` is the process's name (`<process>` in HTTP).

## Write what you read

A pull reads the vendor from where the last run stopped, which the connector keeps in its state document, and writes what it read. [Upsert items in bulk](/api-reference/items/bulkUpsertItems) writes up to 5,000 records in one request:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
POST /items/bulk
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "items": [
    {
      "type": "tasks.task",
      "source_id": "acct-7:4012",
      "tier": "feed",
      "properties": { "task_id": "4012", "title": "Renew passport", "status": "not_started" },
      "occurred_at": "2026-10-01T08:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "atomic": false
}
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.POST("/items/bulk", {
  body: {
    items: [
      {
        type: "tasks.task",
        source_id: "acct-7:4012",
        tier: "feed",
        properties: { task_id: "4012", title: "Renew passport", status: "not_started" },
        occurred_at: "2026-10-01T08:00:00Z",
      },
    ],
    atomic: false,
  },
});
```

Marfa answers each record on its own:

```json title="Response" status="200"
{
  "counts": { "created": 1, "updated": 0, "skipped": 0, "errored": 0 },
  "results": [{ "index": 0, "outcome": "created", "id": "01a12313-fd4a-78a1-af1e-32792c3df63b" }]
}
```

An item's natural key is its `source`, from the connector's key, and its `source_id`, the vendor's own ID for the record. Marfa updates the item that holds the key, or creates one, so reading a record twice never makes a second item. Put the **vendor account** inside the `source_id`, as in `acct-7:4012`, so that two accounts under one source can't share an item.

`tier: "feed"` puts the item in the feed, where a person or an app decides whether to keep it. `occurred_at` is when the record happened at the vendor. `atomic: false` writes the records that pass and reports a refused one as `errored`; by default, one refused record **rolls the whole batch back**.

**Write an item's text as Markdown.** Marfa stores the field its type names in [`display_hints.body_field`](/catalog/type-rules#display-hints) unchecked, so convert a vendor's HTML first, or an app shows the tags.

## Write only what changed

A write of the properties an item already holds **still raises its `version`** and announces `item.updated`, so a pull that rewrites every record makes noise for everyone who follows the event stream.

Before you write, [look up the items](/api-reference/items/lookupItems) you hold under the records' keys and **send only the records that differ**:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
POST /items/lookup
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "type": "tasks.task", "source": "tasks", "source_ids": ["acct-7:4012", "acct-7:4013"] }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.POST("/items/lookup", {
  body: { type: "tasks.task", source: "tasks", source_ids: ["acct-7:4012", "acct-7:4013"] },
});
```

Two cases need care:

- **An item in the bin:** a record that matches it comes back `skipped`, with the reason `trashed`.
- **A purged item:** it leaves a tombstone, which the lookup returns beside the items. Write a purged record again only if the vendor changed it after the tombstone's `settled_at`.

## Set aside what the vendor deleted

When the vendor no longer has a record, [change the item's state](/api-reference/items/transitionItem) to `archived`. **Don't move it to the bin**: the bin is for people, and an archived item keeps its history and can be made active again if the record comes back.

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
POST /items/01a12313-fd4e-7800-ab67-c886f1b9ef58/transition
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "state": "archived" }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.POST("/items/{id}/transition", {
  params: { path: { id: "01a12313-fd4e-7800-ab67-c886f1b9ef58" } },
  body: { state: "archived" },
});
```

Be **sure the vendor deleted it**: a partial listing, such as open tasks only, says nothing about a record it leaves out, so ask about that record first.

## Watch for changes made in Marfa

The items a connector writes are ordinary items, and people and apps edit, archive and move them to the bin. To learn of those changes, follow [the event stream](/api-reference/event-stream/streamEvents) for your type:

```http title="Request"
GET /events?type=tasks.task
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Last-Event-ID: 11
```

Each change arrives as an event with the item as it now stands. `Last-Event-ID` resumes after the last event you handled, so keep that cursor in the state document. [Keep a copy in sync](/build/keep-in-sync) explains the stream.

Your own writes **come back on the stream too**. To tell a person's change from your own, keep an agreement for each item: what the connector and the vendor last agreed it holds. After every write you make or carry, [write the agreement](/api-reference/connector-state/writeConnectorAgreements), under the connector's hold, as [Holds and retries](/build/connector-holds-and-retries) shows:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
POST /connectors/01a12313-d219-7e92-8869-1f6546b43dbc/agreements
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "process": "<process>",
  "set": [
    {
      "item_id": "01a12313-fd4a-78a1-af1e-32792c3df63b",
      "waiting": false,
      "record": { "title": "Renew passport", "status": "not_started" }
    }
  ]
}
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.POST("/connectors/{id}/agreements", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId } },
  body: {
    process: processName,
    set: [
      {
        item_id: "01a12313-fd4a-78a1-af1e-32792c3df63b",
        waiting: false,
        record: { title: "Renew passport", status: "not_started" },
      },
    ],
  },
});
```

When an event arrives, [look up the item's agreement](/api-reference/connector-state/lookupConnectorAgreements) and compare:

- **The item matches the `record`:** the change is one you already agreed, such as your own write.
- **The item differs:** someone changed it in Marfa. Write the agreement again with `waiting` set to **`true`** and the `record` unchanged, so it still says what was agreed and now says a change waits for the vendor.

Record the change **before you move the cursor** past its event. A stop between the two then reads the same event again and finds the agreement already waiting; the other way round, a stop loses the change.

## Carry a change back

[List the agreements](/api-reference/connector-state/listConnectorAgreements) that are waiting:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
GET /connectors/01a12313-d219-7e92-8869-1f6546b43dbc/agreements?waiting=true
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.GET("/connectors/{id}/agreements", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId }, query: { waiting: "true" } },
});
```

```json title="Response" status="200"
{
  "data": [
    {
      "item_id": "01a12313-fd4a-78a1-af1e-32792c3df63b",
      "waiting": true,
      "record": { "title": "Renew passport", "status": "not_started" },
      "updated_at": "2026-10-09T23:51:35.911Z"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

For each one:

1. Read the item.
2. Send the vendor what changed.
3. Once the vendor has taken it, write the agreement with `waiting` set to `false` and a `record` of what both sides now hold.

If the vendor refuses the change or doesn't answer, leave the agreement waiting, say why in the run's report, and try again on the next run. **Never clear** a waiting agreement to move on: the change would be forgotten.

### Send a new item to the vendor

A person can also make an item of your type in Marfa, and a two-way connector creates it at the vendor. The type's `link_field` names the property that holds the vendor's ID for the record. Marfa keeps the value unique within the type, refusing a second item with it as `409 link_taken`.

An item with **no value there** is one the vendor hasn't been told about. For each one:

1. Create the record at the vendor, sending the item's `id` as the vendor's idempotency key if it takes one, so that a retry can't create it twice.
2. [Update the item](/api-reference/items/updateItem) to set the link to the vendor's ID, sending the `version` you read.
3. Write the item's agreement.

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
PATCH /items/01a12314-5e6a-7687-b04c-d62fa7beeccb
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 1, "properties": { "task_id": "4020" } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id: "01a12314-5e6a-7687-b04c-d62fa7beeccb" } },
  body: { version: 1, properties: { task_id: "4020" } },
});
```

Set the link **straight after the vendor answers**. A run that stops between the two sends the same create again, which an idempotency key answers with the record already made. [Register a type](/api-reference/types/registerType) describes `link_field`.

## Rare cases

### Settle a conflict

When a person changes a field in Marfa while the vendor changes the same field, both the item and the vendor differ from the agreement's `record`. One side has to win, and **Marfa doesn't decide which**: choose a rule and apply it every time.

The kit decides by time. **The later change wins**, comparing when the vendor says it changed the record with when the change in Marfa was first seen, and a tie goes to Marfa. A field that changed on only one side takes that side's value.

### Carry a purge to a vendor that can't delete

Change the record instead, such as by closing the task, then [settle the tombstone](/api-reference/items/settleTombstones) to the time of that change. Otherwise the next pull reads the change and brings the record back as a new item.

The rules behind this page are in the [connectors](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/connectors.md) and [items](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/items.md) chapters of the contract.
